tested_scope: Exactly one deterministic self-local replay extending the prior prepared-transition/write-order result. The fixture places one logical external effect between durable prepared transition S2 and repository acknowledgement, then compares two acknowledgement-loss/retry traces. Trace A has no provider-side idempotency or result reconstruction guarantee. Trace B uses one stable provider idempotency token bound to S2 plus exact payload digest and supports replay/readback of the original result. No concrete provider, public source, O/downstream/other-worker state, shared ledger, scheduler mutation, hosted compute, richer-mode arbitration, finite quota, or second semantic leaf is tested.

baseline.crash_boundary: external logical effect occurs after S2 is durable but before repository result acknowledgement is durable

steps: persist S2 prepared with exact payload digest D3 and authority E3
invoke external effect; effect occurs once
repository acknowledgement/result write is lost before durability
next invocation reconstructs S2=prepared with no durable result and retries the same requested effect
trace_A_no_provider_idempotency.observation: Repository state cannot distinguish 'effect never happened' from 'effect happened but acknowledgement was lost'. Retrying can produce a second logical effect; refusing to retry can permanently lose the useful result.

steps: persist S2 prepared with exact payload digest D3 and authority E3
derive one stable provider token T=H(S2,D3) and use it for the external effect
external effect occurs once; repository acknowledgement/result write is lost
next invocation reconstructs S2 and retries/queries with the exact same token T and payload digest
provider returns the same accepted operation/result identity without creating a second logical effect
persist result identity/digest, CAS predecessor to superseded_by=S2, then commit S2 and expose successor only when the predecessor-transition-successor triad matches
trace_B_stable_provider_idempotency_and_.observation: Under the stated abstract provider contract, acknowledgement loss is duplicate-safe because the stable token identifies the already accepted logical effect and the original result can be reconstructed before finalization.

derived_minimum_provider_side_evidence: One idempotency/effect token stable across invocations and retries, derived from or durably bound to the exact transition/effect identity rather than a per-attempt value.
Exact request/payload binding: reuse of the token with a different payload must be rejected rather than silently creating or mutating an effect.
A provider-visible accepted-operation identity or equivalent result handle that can be reconstructed after acknowledgement loss.
Replay/query semantics that return the original accepted result or an unambiguous terminal status without issuing a second logical effect.
Sufficient retention/lifetime for the token and result to survive the repository checkpoint/resume interval being claimed; otherwise safety becomes time-window dependent and remains unresolved.

Repository finalization must still require matching prepared transition, predecessor CAS, provider result identity/digest, and successor binding; provider idempotency alone does not authorize successor visibility.

weak_retry_rule.rule: If S2 is prepared and no repository acknowledgement exists, retry the external action once and then treat the latest response as authoritative.
weak_retry_rule.falsification: Trace A produces two possible logical effects after one lost acknowledgement, while refusing the retry leaves an indistinguishable successful first effect unreconstructed. Therefore repository acknowledgement absence alone is not a safe retry predicate.

observations: A durable prepared transition plus a missing repository acknowledgement leaves an irreducible local ambiguity once an external effect may already have happened.
A stable provider-side effect token removes duplicate issuance only if retries are bound to the identical payload/effect identity.

Useful outcome reconstruction additionally needs a replayable result or unambiguous accepted-operation status; duplicate suppression alone is not enough to recover the result needed for repository finalization.
The idempotency/result retention window is part of the safety scope: if it can expire before the next recurring invocation, the same unknown-outcome ambiguity can reappear.
inference: For the exact abstract acknowledgement-loss fixture tested, repository-local CAS and prepared-transition records are necessary but not sufficient once the logical effect crosses an external boundary. Duplicate-safe recovery requires a provider-side idempotency/effect identity that is stable across invocations, bound to the exact payload, and paired with reconstructible result/terminal-status evidence for at least the claimed checkpoint-resume horizon. This does not prove any concrete Chat-exposed provider supplies those semantics or that the full Phase-1 root is satisfied.
